questions.question: Attention in seq2seq lets the decoder:
options: Use a weighted combination of all encoder hidden states at each step
Use only the last encoder state
questions.explanation: Weights change per output step, focusing on relevant input words.

questions.question: Scaled dot-product attention is:
questions.explanation: Vaswani et al., 2017.

questions.question: Why divide by √d_k?
options: Large dot products push softmax into regions with tiny gradients
questions.explanation: Dot products grow with dimension; scaling keeps softmax well behaved.

questions.question: Attention weights for one query:
questions.explanation: They come from a softmax.

questions.question: In self-attention, Q, K and V come from:
questions.explanation: Cross-attention: Q from decoder, K and V from encoder.

questions.question: A transformer has d_model = 512 and 8 heads. Dimension per head?
Why does a transformer need positional encodings?
options: Self-attention by itself has no notion of token order
questions.explanation: Without them, shuffled words would give the same representations.

questions.question: Masked self-attention in the decoder prevents:
options: Each position from attending to future tokens
questions.explanation: Keeps generation autoregressive.

questions.question: Computation of self-attention grows with sequence length n as:
questions.explanation: Every token attends to every token.

questions.question: Which property lets transformers train much faster than RNNs on GPUs?
questions.explanation: No step-by-step dependency in the encoder.

questions.question: "Attention Is All You Need" (2017) introduced:
questions.explanation: Vaswani et al., Google.

questions.question: Each transformer sub-layer is wrapped with:
options: A residual connection and layer normalisation
questions.explanation: Add & Norm.

questions.question: BERT is:
options: Encoder-only, trained with masked language modelling
questions.explanation: Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers.

questions.question: GPT models are:
questions.explanation: Generative Pre-trained Transformer.

questions.question: Which model family is encoder–decoder? (select all)
questions.explanation: BERT is encoder-only; GPT-3 is decoder-only.

questions.question: Best fit for classifying customer emails into categories (no generation needed):
options: Decoder-only model is the only option
questions.explanation: Encoders give rich bidirectional representations for understanding tasks.

questions.question: In cross-attention of the original transformer, the keys and values come from:
questions.explanation: Queries come from the decoder.

questions.question: Multi-head attention is useful because:
options: Different heads can focus on different relationships
It removes the need for softmax
questions.explanation: Heads run in parallel on lower-dimensional projections, outputs concatenated.

questions.question: Raw scores q·k for two keys are 6 and 0, with d_k = 9. After scaling, the scores are:
questions.explanation: Divide by √9 = 3.

questions.question: Scaled scores are 1 and 1 for two keys with values 4 and 8. Attention output = ?
questions.explanation: Equal scores → weights 0.5, 0.5 → 0.5·4 + 0.5·8 = 6.

questions.question: Bahdanau attention is also called:
questions.explanation: It scores with a small feed-forward network; Luong introduced multiplicative (dot) scoring.

questions.question: The position-wise feed-forward network in a transformer layer is applied:
options: Once to the whole sequence jointly
Separately and identically to each position
questions.explanation: Same two-layer MLP for each position.

questions.question: The original transformer encoder had how many stacked layers?
questions.explanation: 6 encoder + 6 decoder layers; BERT-base has 12.

questions.question: Which statements about transformers are true? (select all)
options: Self-attention cost is quadratic in length
questions.explanation: Transformers are used for text, images (ViT), audio and more.
